```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_bslib <- requireNamespace("bslib", quietly = TRUE) && utils::packageVersion("bslib") >= "0.6.0"
```

```{r}
library(hovercraft)
```

## Nothing to do on a bslib page

The tips read Bootstrap's variables where the page has them, so a page built with `bslib::page_fluid()` and a
`bslib::bs_theme()` already has tips in the theme's colours, corner and font, and they turn dark with
`bslib::input_dark_mode()` on their own. The tip is a shade of the page: a little darker than a light page and a little lighter than a dark one, in
Bootstrap's tertiary background with the page's own text colour. A small arrow points from the tip to its tag.

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "48%", fig.alt = "A button with a tip below it and a small arrow between them, a pale grey tip on a light page and a dark grey tip on a dark page.", fig.show = "hold"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("figures/default-light.png", "figures/default-dark.png"))
```

Use a theme when the tips must look different from the page, when the brand is not in a `bs_theme()`, or when the page
has no bslib.

## Your own roles

`tip_theme()` takes named roles, in a list for light and one for dark. A role you leave out keeps what the page gives.

| Role | What it sets | Takes |
|---|---|---|
| `bg` | the tip's fill | a colour |
| `ink` | its words | a colour |
| `line` | its border, seen in forced-colours mode and in a tip that stays open | a colour |
| `code_bg` | behind code | a colour |
| `radius` | the corner | pixels, or a length such as `"0.5rem"` |
| `shadow` | the shadow | CSS `box-shadow` text, or `"none"` |
| `font` | the typeface | CSS `font-family` text |

```{r}
brand <- tip_theme(
  light = list(bg = "#1b3a6b", ink = "#ffffff", radius = 10, shadow = "0 6px 18px rgba(27, 58, 107, 0.35)"),
  dark = list(bg = "#9ec5fe", ink = "#0b1f3a")
)
brand
```

A role set in `light` and not in `dark` is used in dark mode too, so a brand colour set once holds in both modes.
Colours may be names, hex, `rgb()` text or three numbers from 0 to 255. Give the theme to `tip_dependency()` as `style`
once, in the page's UI:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ui <- bslib::page_fluid(
  tip_dependency(style = brand),
  tip_on(actionButton("go", "Run"), "Runs the **check**")
)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "48%", fig.alt = "The same button with a navy tip with a small arrow, rounded and shadowed, on a light page, and a pale blue tip on a dark page.", fig.show = "hold"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("figures/theme-light.png", "figures/theme-dark.png"))
```

### Light and dark

`mode = "auto"` (the default) follows the page: the `data-bs-theme` attribute that `bslib::input_dark_mode()` sets on the
page, and, when the page names none, the visitor's own setting. `"light"` and `"dark"` use that mode whatever the page says.
A tip is drawn at the page level, so a `data-bs-theme` on a smaller part of the page does not reach it.

## Presets and styles

A preset is a named look the engine ships: a corner, a font, colours for light and dark and a shadow. `tip_presets()` lists
them, and a name is all `style` needs:

```{r}
tip_presets()[c("name", "label")]
tip_dependency(style = "sober")[[2]]$name
```

`style` takes a preset name, `"none"` (clears a preset set further out), a `tip_style()`, or one part of a style, such as a
`tip_theme()`. `tip_style()` bundles a preset, a theme and a class for the tip box: `tip_style("sober", theme = brand)` is
sober with the roles of `brand` changed. A string that holds `:` or `;` is not a style: `style` takes no CSS, and a list
goes to `tip_theme()` or `tip_style(theme = list(...))`.

A tag can have its own look. `tip_on(btn, "Run", style = "dense")` beats the page's style for that tag, and a value set
nearer wins, value by value: a tag whose theme sets only `bg` keeps the page's `ink`. A preset on a tag replaces the
page's preset as a whole, and a theme beats a preset set at the same place or further out.

The tips of a table take a look the same way: `tip_table(style = "sober")` styles all of them, and a column's
`tip_spec("{{ note }}", style = "dense")` gives that column its own, keeping what it does not set from the table. A row's
own style also reaches the cells of that row that have none of their own.

`class` puts class names on the tip box, for your own CSS. The nearest class wins as a whole (a tag's `class = "wide"`
replaces the page's `class = "brand"`), and `class = ""` clears one:

```{r}
tip_style("sober", class = c("wide", "audit-tip"))
```

## Markers

A tip is out of sight until the pointer rests on its tag, so a reader cannot tell which words hold one. A marker is a
visible cue on the tag, off by default and chosen for each tag with `marker =`:

```{r}
tip_on(htmltools::tags$span("Baseline", tabindex = "0"), "The first **screening** value", marker = "underline")
```

`"underline"` draws a line under the words and takes no room, `"icon"` adds a small icon after them, and `"corner"`
draws a small triangle in the top corner, as a spreadsheet does for a note. It suits a table cell or a value box; on a
word it can look like a stray mark. Markers are drawn in the tag's own text colour, so they keep its contrast in light
and dark, and the pointer over a marked tag is the help cursor.

The line of an underline follows the preset: dotted for `"none"`, `"sober"` and `"dense"`, dashed for `"modern"` and
`"editorial"`, and a long gentle wave for `"lively"`. `tip_marker()` chooses one yourself, or gives your own icon, as a
tag:

```{r}
tip_marker("underline", line = "wavy")
tip_marker("icon", icon = htmltools::tags$b("?"))
```

An icon from `fontawesome::fa()` or `bsicons::bs_icon()` works the same way, and `marker = <icon>` is short for
`tip_marker("icon", icon = <icon>)`. An icon is added to the tag as a child that a
screen reader skips; a name such as `"info"` is not looked up, because the package does not pick an icon library for you.
For an underline on a block tag (a table cell, a paragraph), the words are put in a `span` so the line goes under them and
not across the cell. A value box marks its title. A block of other tags has no words to underline, so it stops with an error that says where the marker goes.

In a table, `tip_table(marker = "corner")` marks every cell and header cell that has a tip, in `DT` and `reactable`;
a `tip_spec(marker = )` marks or unmarks one column. Only the corner is drawn there for now, and a row takes no marker.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
DT::datatable(scores) |>
  tip_table(cells = c(wins = "{{ wins }} wins"), headers = c(wins = "Games won"), marker = "corner")
```

## A bslib theme

A `bslib::bs_theme()` is read through its variables (bslib 0.6.0 or later): the tip's fill is the theme's tertiary background, its words
the theme's text colour, with the border colour, corner and font. This is for a page that is not built with the theme; a page
that is needs no theme at all.

```{r, eval = has_bslib}
warm <- bslib::bs_theme(
  version = 5,
  bg = "#fdf6e3",
  fg = "#073642",
  "border-radius" = "0.6rem",
  "body-bg-dark" = "#002b36",
  "body-color-dark" = "#eee8d5"
)
tip_dependency(style = warm)[[2]]$name
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "48%", fig.alt = "A button with a tip below it in pale cream with dark teal words, rounded corners and a small arrow, then the same in dark mode with a muted teal tip.", fig.show = "hold"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("figures/bs-theme-light.png", "figures/bs-theme-dark.png"))
```

## CSS variables

A named list whose names all start with `--` sets CSS variables as they are, for both modes: the engine's own variables, or
any variable the page's CSS defines. Give it to `tip_style(theme = )`: a bare list is not taken as `style`, because a style
has more parts than a theme.

```{r}
tip_dependency(style = tip_style(theme = list("--hovercraft-tip-radius" = "4px")))[[2]]$name
```

These variables reach the tips from the page only, not from one tag.

A role can also read a variable: `tip_theme(light = list(bg = "--team-blue"))` reads `--team-blue` where the page defines
it. R cannot check the value of a variable; the browser works it out.

## Contrast

The words of a tip must be readable on its fill. For each mode `tip_theme()` measures the `ink` on the `bg` (and on the
`code_bg`, if you give one). Below 4.5:1, the usual level for text, it warns and keeps the colours. A role you leave out is taken
to be what a bslib page gives by default: Bootstrap's tertiary background with the page's text colour, in that mode.

```{r}
tip_theme(light = list(bg = "#ffffff", ink = "#dddddd")) |>
  suppressWarnings() |>
  invisible()
```

The warning has the class `hovercraft_contrast`. Turn the warnings off with `options(hovercraft.contrast_warnings = FALSE)`, or
silence only them with `withCallingHandlers(..., hovercraft_contrast = function(w) invokeRestart("muffleWarning"))`.
